primitive: exploratory factor analysis (minres, principal axis) with rotation
r_function: psych::fa(r = R, nfactors = k, fm = 'minres' | 'pa', rotate = 'none', n.obs = n_star); stats::varimax, stats::promax(m = 4), GPArotation::oblimin(gam = 0) on the unrotated loadings
note: R = the fixture's listwise (weighted) correlation; n_star = N / sum(w) / Kish n_eff. minres = psych's L-BFGS-B fit (stops early); minres_exact = its exact optimum, the principal-axis fixed point (fm = 'pa', min.err = 1e-14). principal_axis = psych's default iteration (SMC start, min.err 0.001, max.iter 50; converged = fewer than 50 iterations). unrotated = psych's loadings, columns flipped to sum positive; communalities = rowSums(L^2), uniquenesses = 1 - communalities, variance = colSums(L^2). rotations = Pulse's engine definitions put through rot_canon (descending variance diag(Phi L'L), then each column summing positive); psych::fa's own varimax / oblimin asserted equal; psych's 'promax' (kaiser + GPArotation::Varimax) is not stats::promax and is not used. rmsr / empirical_chisq / df / empirical_p = psych fa.stats rms / chi / dof / EPVAL (asserted); objective = sum_{i != j} res^2. kmo = psych::KMO; bartlett = psych::cortest.bartlett(R, n = n_star). The heywood case has no exact optimum (its minres optimum is improper) and is compared on detection only.
